title: Kinnikuman: Kessen! Shichinin no Seigi Choujin vs. Uchuu Nobushi
summary: A 72-minute Nippon TV golden-time special (土曜トップスペシャル, Sat 19:30-20:54, 1984-04-07) that animates the one block of Yudetamago's manga the TV run skipped: the 宇宙野武士編 / ラッカ星防衛編, printed chapters 86-89 (「宇宙からの使者の巻」「七人の超人の巻」「ラッカ星のかくし砦の巻」「７人対怪物の巻」, all inside JC vol 7 = ch 81-94). THE PREMISE HELD, re-derived on primaries: ja-WP's arc list gives 第2次怪獣退治編（第80話 - 第89話） and says アニメ版ではカットされている（宇宙野武士編は内容を改変した上でアニメスペシャルとして放映）, its TV article レギュラー放送ではカットされたラッカ星防衛編をアニメ化したもの; the Kinnikuman Wiki's arc infobox prints chapter = 80-89 / anime = TV Special, Movie 2 and its Beansman page cites ch 86/87/88/89 beat by beat; and 加山竜司's dated per-volume review names those four chapter titles as the 宇宙野武士編 and places them in vol 7 between 「ベルトか日本救出か!?の巻」 (vol 6's last = ch 80) and 「ライバルは日本にいたの巻」 (ch 90, which opens the Olympics arc). The special's first act IS ch 86-87 — Rakka overrun, the elder Ingen sending Beansman to Earth, Terryman tested with a monster, Ramenman recruited, Kinnikuman muscling in uninvited, the seven assembled, the ship leaving for Rakka — and its ending is ch 89's outcome, with the Space Bandits' two defining gimmicks intact (they break off a war to eat; they split into copies) and the heart still their weak point. But a story-carrying ORIGINAL share sits beside it, and ja-WP catalogues it itself under アニメオリジナルシリーズ: seven NAMED anime-original Space Bandits (Black King, Black Tomahawk, Black Kung Fu, Black Knight, Black Fighter, Black Killer, Black Sumoman) fought as 「1対1のリング上での決闘を同時に行う」 — a seven-ring 団体戦 the manga has no trace of — plus Princess Marron, an anime-original ruler of Rakka whom Black King abducts into a forced wedding that Kinnikuman crashes (風林火山 → キン肉バスター), plus Beansman's late reveal that he is really 「キンギョ星」の「メダカ王子」 and his marriage to Marron, plus Ramenman staying behind on Rakka. Two of the manga's seven (Puyo-Puyo, Crystalman) and ch 88's whole fortress-and-hiding-villagers setup are gone, replaced by Robin Mask, Warsman and Rikishiman and by four original recruitment duels (Robin vs two knights, Warsman vs the anime-original Robo Chojin in a Siberian snowstorm, Brocken Jr. and Rikishiman vs tanks). Roughly half the first act and most of the second half is material the chapters do not contain: a substantial source share beside a substantial original share, so under T28 the standing is mixed. Surprise for the file: during the Dream Chojin Tag arc Yudetamago drew the SPECIAL's roster into the source line as a 扉絵 — the title page of 「ハリケーン・ヒート!!の巻」 (WSJ 1984 #18, JC vol 21 p.7) shows Robin Mask, Warsman and Wolfman, none of whom is in the manga's arc. That is an anime announcement in drawn form — designs without events — so it is a credit, never an adoption (T26).

chapters_adapted.note: The special's entire first act. Ch 86 「宇宙からの使者の巻」 (12 pp): the Space Bandits overrun Planet Rakka, the elder Ingen takes an arrow through the head and sends his pupil Beansman to Earth for Justice Chojin, Beansman tests Terryman with a monster and recruits Ramenman, Kinnikuman hears and forces himself into the group. Ch 87 「七人の超人の巻」 (12 pp): the recruiting tour completes the seven and they leave for Rakka. Every one of those beats is in the special (dAnime/Toei's own synopsis: インゲン長老はビーンズマンに地球へ向かうよう指示する … テリーマンたちアイドル超人の協力を得ることに成功する。一方のキン肉マンも、自分だけ呼ばれないことを気にかけて、進んで助っ人の仲間入りを果たす). ALTERED, not omitted: the order is inverted (Beansman tests Kinnikuman FIRST and writes him off — ja-WP's Beansman entry), Ingen is recast as a 国務大臣 who hands over a LIST of candidates instead of dying in the escape, and Puyo-Puyo and Crystalman are swapped for Robin Mask, Warsman and Rikishiman with four original test-duels. The chapters' job — assemble the seven and get them to Rakka — is the special's job, so this segment carries weight.

The journey, the enemy's defining gimmicks and the arc's resolution. Ch 88 「ラッカ星のかくし砦の巻」 (13 pp) supplies the flight to Rakka and the Space Bandits' rule that they stop a war to eat — in the special that is the reason Kinnikuman's bout with Black King is abandoned mid-match (ja-WP: 団体戦ではキン肉マンと戦うが、昼食時間のために試合を一時放棄). Ch 89 「７人対怪物の巻」 (11 pp) supplies the enemy's 肉体分裂分身の術 (Black Sumoman beats Rikishiman by splitting into five), the heart as their weak point (Terryman kills Black Tomahawk with a knee drop to the heart; Black King is the one bandit with TWO hearts), the seven's combined finishing attack, and the outcome the whole work exists for — the Space Bandits destroyed and Planet Rakka freed. REPLACED: ch 88's hidden fortress, the hiding villagers and the disguised-Ingen reveal (the special gives Rakka a royal court under Princess Marron instead — ja-WP: テレビスペシャルでは、マロン姫が統治している), and ch 89's climax proper (the pieces merging into one giant monster, Ingen's death, Beansman shaking Terryman's hand) — in their place a seven-ring team match, the abduction of Princess Marron and a Kinniku Buster on Black King. Significant because the arc's ending IS the special's ending; the staging is what changed.

position.why: 51.5 is the calendar answer and it is right as a BROADCAST fact — 1984-04-07 (Sat) falls between ep 51 (Sun 1984-04-01) and ep 52 (Sun 1984-04-08) on ja-WP's episode table, which matches our stored dates row for row — but as a watch slot it drops a 72-minute film into the middle of one continuous match (our ep 51 「悪魔超人ブラックホールの巻／戦慄の四次元レスリングの巻」 → ep 52 「影の殺し屋！分身技の巻」 is the same Black Hole fight). Three SOURCED orders put the work at the 47/48 seam instead. (1) SETTING: ja-WP — 原作での時間軸は第21回超人オリンピック前だったが、本作はオリンピック後の設定になっている; the Olympics arc closes on ep 47 「史上初! V2の巻」 and ja-WP's own table puts the ７人の悪魔超人編 header between rows 47 and 48. (2) STATED VIEWING ORDER: the Kinnikuman Wiki's 'Anime Timeline' page ('This is the intended viewing order of the Kinnikuman anime') lists the TV Special between '21st Chojin Olympics Arc (eps 27-47)' and 'Seven Akuma Chojin Arc (eps 48-65)', and the special's own page carries previous = Episode 47B / next = Episode 48A. (3) LICENSOR: Toei Video's DVD line breaks at exactly that seam — Vol.4 = eps 37-47 (11 eps, 271 min) and Vol.5 = eps 48-56 (9 eps, 295 min); every one of the twelve volumes runs 24.50-24.67 min per episode except Vol.5 at 32.78, an excess of 73 minutes that is this special, so the special ships on the disc that OPENS the Devil Chojin arc. Nothing in the special needs eps 48-51 (Warsman debuts ep 29B, Rikishiman ep 27, Brocken Jr. before ep 47; the VA is Ryoichi Tanaka, eps 47-58). See the position flag: if the halo's field is meant to record the broadcast slot rather than the watch slot, 51.5 is correct and this is a confirmation.

flags_for_sean: PREMISE HELD, RE-DERIVED (R3). The wave-2 triage's 'printed ch 86-89, vol 7' reproduces from three independent lineages: ja-WP (arc list 第2次怪獣退治編 = 第80話-第89話 + 宇宙野武士編は内容を改変した上でアニメスペシャルとして放映 + レギュラー放送ではカットされたラッカ星防衛編をアニメ化したもの); the Kinnikuman Wiki (arc infobox chapter = 80-89 / anime = TV Special, Movie 2; Beansman's history cites ch 86/87/88/89 individually with the beats); and 加山竜司's per-volume review, which defines 宇宙野武士編 as exactly 「宇宙からの使者の巻」「七人の超人の巻」「ラッカ星のかくし砦の巻」「七人対怪物の巻」. Nothing was inherited.

VOLUME CONVERSION SHOWN AT BOTH EDGES, ONE EDITION. The chapter numbers are the PRINTED original-run numbering (WSJ 1979 #22 - 1987 #21; ja-WP 話数 = 全387話（36巻まで）). Jump Comics vol 7 「ライバルは日本にいたの巻」 (1981-09-15; 新装版 ISBN 978-4-08-870731-0) = ch 081-094 per the Kinnikuman Wiki's volume-contents table, and three checks confirm both edges: Kayama says vol 6's last chapter is 「ベルトか日本救出か!?の巻」 (= ch 080) and vol 7 holds 14 chapters ending after 「富士の最終予選の巻」 (= ch 094); Shueisha's own copy for that ISBN carries BOTH the Rakka story and the start of the Olympics (地球に瓜二つのラッカ星を、宇宙野武士が襲撃。彼らを撃退するため、七人の超人が手を組んだ！　さらに、超人オリンピック ザ・ビッグファイトの開催も決定); and the TITLE TEST passes on the chapter numbers either side of the range (086 宇宙からの使者, 089 ７人対怪物, 090 ライバルは日本にいた = ja-WP's Olympics-arc opener). Kayama also dates ch 88 to WSJ 1981 #11 and ch 90 to #13, so 86-90 are contiguous with no phantom slot. NO source shift to apply.

POSITION FORK — YOUR CALL. Two answers, both sourced, answering different questions. WATCH SLOT = 47.5 (what I propose): ja-WP says the special was re-set to AFTER the 21st Chojin Olympics, the Kinnikuman Wiki's 'Anime Timeline' page names it the intended viewing order and puts the special between eps 27-47 and eps 48-65, the special's page reads previous = Episode 47B / next = Episode 48A, and Toei Video's DVD line breaks at 47/48 with the special bundled onto Vol.5. BROADCAST SLOT = 51.5 (what is stored): the special aired 1984-04-07 between ep 51 (04-01) and ep 52 (04-08), and a contemporaneous viewer records that the TV run was 'around the point Stecase King was beaten' when it aired (eps 50-51). The two differ by four rows and the broadcast slot lands mid-match. If the halo field is defined as air order, treat this row as CONFIRMED at 51.5 instead — nothing else in the verdict changes.

DATE CONFIRMED, NOT REPAIRED. 1984-04-07 stands on ja-WP twice (the TV article's テレビスペシャル section and the 土曜トップスペシャル programme list), on the ja Kinnikuman Fandom (1984年（昭和59年）4月7日放送), and on Kayama's dated article. Day-of-week test: 1984-04-07 is a SATURDAY, which is the 土曜トップスペシャル 19:30-20:54 slot; AniList's 1984-07-04 is a Wednesday and cannot be. DO NOT cite the EN Kinnikuman Wiki's 'April 6, 1984' — that column is one day EARLY run-wide (its ep 2 = April 9 1983 and every following row is a Saturday against a Sunday broadcast; its ep 47 = March 3 vs ja-WP's 3月4日, its ep 52 = April 7 vs 4月8日). April 6 is that same -1 applied to April 7, not a rival reading.

T26 — CREDIT, NOT ADOPTION; adopted stays null. Yudetamago's screen credit is the ordinary 原作; the screenplay is 山崎晴哉's. The one thing that comes close is a drawn page IN the source line: during the Dream Chojin Tag arc's serialization the author put an 宇宙野武士編 image-scene 扉絵 on 「ハリケーン・ヒート!!の巻」 (WSJ 1984 #18, on sale 4/16, nine days after broadcast; collected JC vol 21 p.7, cited by ja-WP), and it depicts Robin Mask, Warsman and Wolfman — the SPECIAL's roster, none of whom is in the manga's arc. That is an anime announcement in illustration form: designs without events, exactly the shape T26 excludes. Recorded here so it is not re-discovered later as an adoption claim.

SOLE ANIMATED COVERAGE OF A SKIPPED BLOCK. Printed ch 80-89 was cut from the TV run wholesale (ja-WP's arc list; Kayama: この「怪獣退治編（第二次）」は、アニメ化の際にはカットされた; our own rows agree — ep 26 closes the American Tour and ep 27 opens the 21st Olympics = ch 90). Inside that block only Movie 2 (ch 82-83, per the wave-2 triage) and this special (86-89) reach the screen at all, so ch 80, 81, 84 and 85 are animated NOWHERE in the catalogue. This special is the only way a viewer ever sees ch 86-89.

SHARE ESTIMATE IS A BEAT COUNT, NOT A STOPWATCH. I could not obtain a timecoded synopsis; the 'roughly half the first act, most of the second half is original' reading is assembled from ja-WP's per-character accounts (the seven named Space Bandits and their seven match results, Princess Marron, Ingen's recast role, Beansman's Prince Medaka reveal), the ja Fandom's オリジナルキャラクター list, and one eyewitness blog that names the five recruitment test-battles and the 後半 match card. Both halves are independently attested, which is why the standing is high confidence; the split itself is an estimate. A timecode pass on the Toei disc would settle it.

TITLE ALIAS, NOT A REPAIR. The broadcast title is 「キン肉マン 決戦!7人の正義超人vs宇宙野武士」 (ja-WP; the Toei Complete DVD-BOX contents list uses it too), which is what AniList and our row carry. Every current streaming licensee prints a different rendering — 「キン肉マン 決戦!! 七人の超人VS宇宙野武士」 (dAnime, U-NEXT, Hulu, Prime Video, videomarket). Also: dAnime serves the special as '全4話' (Chapter.1-4) with the SAME one-paragraph synopsis on all four parts — a streaming re-cut, not act markers and not an episode count.

SOURCE INDEPENDENCE. I treated ja-Wikipedia and kinnikuman.fandom.com/ja as ONE lineage (the ja Fandom's 概要 for this work is near-verbatim ja-WP, as the wave-2 triage found) and leaned on kinnikuman.fandom.com (EN) for the independent chapter/character reading. The licensor tier is Toei Video + Toei Animation + dAnime (one lineage, Toei). dic.pixiv.net (via a fetch proxy; the live page is Cloudflare-403) and the ameblo review are CROSS-CHECK ONLY — no claim above rests on either alone, though pixiv's 「TVスペシャルのため7人の悪魔超人編が始まるDVDに収録され」 independently matches the Toei Vol.5 runtime arithmetic.

OUTSIDE THE ASK, NOT RESEARCHED. Our grid has ep 47 → ch 119-120 with continue 122 and ep 48 → 122-123, while ja-WP puts the 21st Olympics arc at ch 90-121 and the Seven Devil Chojin arc at ch 122-159. Our ep 48 START matches the printed arc boundary exactly (a good sign the catalogue is in the printed space), but ch 121 sits unclaimed between rows 47 and 48. Flagging only; I did not check whether ep 47 covers it.
